text:
nora: quick sync — proposing a deterministic 'accrual window' refactor for trace cost attribution. problem: current ingest-window assignment splits multi-chunk/late-enrich traces across windows, causing billing noise and heavy cross-window queries.

nora: idea in one line: compute a stable trace-key -> deterministic window offset; all chunks for that trace fold into the same accrual-window even if spans arrive late.

sam: how do we treat very late spans (beyond a few minutes)? backfill or overflow?

nora: two knobs: window_width (e.g., 5m) and late_horizon (e.g., 1h). within horizon we fold into the accrual window. after horizon, spans go to an overflow bucket with a best-effort attribution tag. overflow still queryable but marked.

maria: migration: customers will notice historical charge diffs. do we dual-write to avoid surprises?

jen: phased rollout suggestion: dual-path for a window (both old and accrual tags) so we can compare diffs, then offer a sampled backfill or opt-in exact reprocess.

alex: implementation question: compute trace-key at edge (fast tagging) or at central gateway (single source of truth)? edge reduces round trips but requires SDK canonicalization; gateway centralizes logic but adds CPU at ingest.

ria: canonicalization must be deterministic: e.g. sha256(tenant|service_fingerprint|root_span) fallback on trace_id when available. spec must include fallback rules and example headers. don't rely on every SDK to be perfect.

sam: index/cardinality concerns: will accrual-key create large cardinality in our index store? any numbers?

nora: it's similar to current active trace count per window; sliding/deterministic mapping shouldn't multiply cardinality — prototype to validate.

jen: testing matrix: out-of-order spans, chunked traces, late enrich >1h, cross-region fanout. need query perf comparison for stitched joins before/after.

ci-bot: queued: accrual-sim -> integration-suite (ETA ~12m) :gear:

maria: backfill cost reduction: do a sampled re-accumulate + extrapolate deltas; only full replay if delta > threshold. cheaper and good for customer communications.

alex: multi-region note: hashing algorithm must be spec'd and identical across regions; include unit tests that seed same inputs.

ria: I'll draft an RFC appendix covering: canonical key algorithm, header names (versioned), window width, late horizon, overflow tag schema, dual-write header format, canary criteria, and sample payloads.

sam: add metric accrual_window_mismatch_rate (cases where same logical trace_id maps to >1 accrual_window). set initial canary threshold 0.1%.

jen: rollout plan: 1) staging prototype 2) canary 5% (non-billed) 3) 25%/50% ramp if metrics good 4) full. include kill-switch.

maria: customer-facing: provide a 7d cost-change-impact diff per account during canary to reduce surprise.

nora: actions: - ria: draft appendix + canonicalization spec (EOD Wed) - alex: spike gateway vs edge tradeoff (this week) - jen: telemetry sim harness (PR by Fri) - sam: add mismatch metric + dashboard - maria: ballpark backfill cost for sampling approach (Thu)

alex: i'll take the gateway spike unless others prefer edge.

ria: sample spec snippet I'll include: ```json
{
  "trace_key": "sha256(tenant|service_fingerprint|root_id)~0x1a2b",
  "accrual_window": "2026-03-22T15:45:00Z/5m",
  "attribution_tag": "accrual-v2"
}
```

sam: nit: use versioned header names like X-Accrual-Key-v1 so older proxies ignore it gracefully.

jen: if CI-proto flakes ping me. happy to help triage. :thumbsup:

nora: thanks all — i'll consolidate and post a short RFC addendum after ria's draft lands.

maria: thanks! this should reduce the billing spikes we've seen. :raised_hands:
